column1: # THE ENVIRONMENT DECLARATION. One row per environment that EXISTS AS A NAME.
# An address is reserved by being declared here, not by something listening on
# it. That is the whole point of the `activated` column: a declared, inactive
# environment still owns its ports, so nothing else can be allocated onto them
# and a reader can see the shape of the estate before it is built. ports.tsv is
# the CMDB of what is RUNNING; this is the map of what is NAMED.
# tier is read off the number and the number is the contract (CLAUDE.md):
#   9100-9199  team       real environments that CANNOT promote
# promotes=no is not a policy toggle. A team environment cannot promote because
# nothing downstream of it reads its verdict -- guard 4 names staging:* and
# production:* observations and nothing else. Setting it to yes would not grant
# the power, it would only make the file lie.
